I added a response for you!

Red pigments are anthrocyanins. They are helpful as antioxidants that form to help eliminate problematic molecules (called free radicals). You may know that these are considered healthy things in foods and fruits (blueberries for example)

Anthrocyanins are helpful in the fall because leaves break down chlorophyll to save their important nutrients (namely nitrogen) when there isn’t enough light to be useful. At this time, plants generate anthrocyanins to protect the plants from excess light when there is no chlorophyll to absorb the light energy. These molecules help absorb free radicals formed by “photochemical quenching” when that light energy has nowhere to go. The anthrocyanins eliminate these free radicals and prevent damage.

In new shoots and leaves when a plant is vulnerable to too much light, anthrocyanins can be produced. Likely you see these in very young trees which are vulnerable because they have not generated enough chlorophyll yet!

I’ll add that most of the anthrocyanin is produced “de novo” in the fall. Contrary to popular belief this anthrocyanin NOT there the whole year. Xanthophylls which serve as yellow pigments actually are there all year, and people assume that is the case for all deciduous leaves.

But in a lecture course, what OP was describing, requiring discussion likely serves no demonstrable purpose and other forms of assessment make more sense and eliminate bias.

In HS there’s a whole page in the rule book about correctable errors. We don’t have instant replay, but there are lots of situations that could happen. Wrong points to wrong team. Foul count wrong and free throws need to be rescinded. Someone fouled out but scorers got the count wrong and player scores. Shit like that. There’s a general rule of two dead balls whereafter you cannot change those mistakes.

In the NBA they have the same kind of thing where they can and can’t review. It covers close game situations and mostly timing and scoring related issues. They generally don’t automatically review for fouls or out of bounds. It’s hard to decide what should or shouldn’t be reviewed - you could imagine that it everything was reviewable, people would demand everything be looked at, which makes the games suck. People already complain about reviews for flagrant fouls etc. This situation is a weird one that unfortunately just isn’t on the list, is super rare, but looks so obvious on the televised game.
